desc: Ideation: confirmed bottom-up greedy with multiset pairing is the correct approach.
Fix the leaf detection in DFS so that a node is considered a leaf only when it has no children (parent excluded), and ensure the root case is handled correctly.
In DFS, handle dangle values from children correctly: child_return == K → count completed and don't add to dangles; 0 < child_return < K → add to dangles.
Replace per-node heap with sorted list and two-pointer pairing (smallest + largest) for optimal O(d log d) merging, avoiding repeated heap rebuilds.
At the root, handle remaining dangle: if length == K count it; if length > 0 fail; ensure completed == N.
Fix the DFS to handle single-dangle closure: close dangles of length K-1 directly, and when one dangle remains after pairing, extend it by 1 (if ==K close, if <K propagate).
Implement the updated DFS logic in the code: separate dangles of length K-1 (close immediately), sort remaining, pair smallest+largest greedily, then handle leftover dangle extension.
Ensure output is exactly "Yes" or "No" (capitalized) to match required format.
Run the solution on Sample 1 and verify it outputs "Yes".
Run the solution on Sample 2 and verify it outputs "No".
Test edge case K=1 with N>1 (any tree) → expect "Yes".
